Here, **your face** represents the presence of the people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before you]

In this clause, the object comes before the verb, unlike the clauses before and after it. If it would be more natural in your language, you could change the order of these words. Alternate translation: [and you shall destroy all the images of their molten metal]

Here, **high places** are a kind of shrine that the people of Canaan built on hilltops for worshiping their gods. If your readers would not be familiar with what high places are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [their hilltop worship sites]

53.q: וְ⁠הוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ וִֽ⁠ישַׁבְתֶּם־בָּ֑⁠הּ כִּ֥י לָ⁠כֶ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ לָ⁠רֶ֥שֶׁת אֹתָֽ⁠הּ
53.note: The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [And you shall possess the land and dwell in it, for this reason: I have given the land to you to possess it]

54.note: The word **you** in the phrase **you shall increase** is plural. The word **you** in the phrase **you shall decrease** is singular. So use the proper singular and plural forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

In both places, the pronoun **it** could refer to: (1) each individual clan. Alternate translation: [for each clan … for that clan] (2) each individual person within a clan. Alternate translation: [for each person … for that person]

Yahweh is using the adjectives **the many** and **the few** as nouns to mean certain kinds of groups of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [For the clans that have many people … and for the clans that have few people]

Yahweh is using **To where it goes out for it** as a common expression of the culture to mean “wherever the lot assigns the land to a clan.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Whatever place falls to a clan]
See how you translated this expression in 26:55.

55.q: וְ⁠אִם־לֹ֨א תוֹרִ֜ישׁוּ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָ⁠אָרֶץ֮ מִ⁠פְּנֵי⁠כֶם֒ וְ⁠הָיָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תּוֹתִ֣ירוּ מֵ⁠הֶ֔ם
55.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that the Israelites might not dispossess the dwellers of the land. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [But suppose that you do not dispossess the dwellers of the land from your face. In that case, whom you leave from them shall be]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people who remained in the land were **splinters in your eyes** and **thorns in your sides**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for a constant source of irritation and painful trouble to you]
